subject: Premium coverage and availability bands — pricing & retainer options
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finlytics.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Premium support bands and discounts

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team at FinLytics is excited about Redwood for our production inference needs. Before we move forward we'd like to get firm pricing around premium support and SLA options so we can scope internally. Specifically: 

- Uptime / availability bands (99.5 / 99.9 / 99.95) and the unit economics ties to each band
- Response time SLAs for P1/P2 (on-call escalation windows and overlap with their timezones)
- Escalation coverage (weekend on-call, named incidents, access to senior engineers)
- Any volume/commit discounts linked to monthly token throughput or reserved capacity

We're targeting a committed 12‑month usage plan and would expect a meaningful discount in exchange for the commit. Can you share a term sheet and a worked example (we'll attach our estimated monthly token curve separately)? Also, what's Redwood's credit policy if SLOs aren't met?

Attachments: FinLytics_Monthly_Estimates.csv (see top sheet for peak windows)

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
FinLytics

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finlytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Premium support bands and discounts

Hi Alyssa — thank you for the clear ask and for sending the estimates. Appreciate the signal on a 12‑month commit.

Quick summary of what I attached: a short term sheet and a worked example based on the numbers you shared. High level options we propose:

1) Availability bands (monthly uptime SLO)
   - Standard: 99.5% — included with hosted API; no retainer required
   - Business: 99.9% — $6,500/mo retainer + per-token price tiers (saves ~10% on per-token compared to Standard)
   - Premium: 99.95% — $18,000/mo retainer + 18% per-token discount + named incident manager and guaranteed 1‑hour P1 response during business hours

2) Response times & escalation
   - P1 (service-down, production impact): phone + Slack within 1 hour (Premium), 2 hours (Business)
   - P2 (degraded performance, high error rate): 4 hours (Premium), 8 hours (Business)
   - 24/7 on-call available as an add-on: $3,000/mo (covers weekend escalation handoff and postmortem support)

3) Credits & penalties
   - Service credits tiered by missed SLO (we include a draft credit matrix in the sheet). Credits are applied to invoice month; we do not provide cash refunds.

4) Commit discounts
   - 12‑month commit: additional 7% off the per-token price on top of the band discount (applies to usage above reserved base).
   - 24‑month commit: 12%

I've looped in Karthik for technical billing details and Olga for contract/compliance items. If this aligns, we can turn the term sheet into a DocuSign and route for signature.

Next steps:
- Karthik: review the worked example and advise on commit sizing and burst allowances
- Olga: prepare a compliance note for SOC2 attestations and audit logs retention for the Premium band
- Alyssa: confirm which availability band you're leaning toward and whether you want 24/7 on-call included

Sending the term sheet and usage calc now.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finlytics.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Premium support bands and discounts

Adding a few specifics from engineering/ops on how the commit & burst model would work for the example load: 

- Reserved baseline: customer picks a monthly token commit (e.g., 4B tokens/month). Reserved usage billed at the committed per-token rate.
- Bursting: short-term burst capacity allowed at an overage rate; for workloads with heavy spiky tails we recommend a burst pool that amortizes cost (we showed a worked amortization in Usage-Band-Calc.xlsx).
- Autoscaling & SLO tie-in: Premium band includes priority scaling lanes and KV cache reservations that reduce cold-start risk during bursts. That operational isolation is what enables 99.95% availability guarantees.

Pricing note: if FinLytics can commit to a minimum monthly baseline above 3B tokens, we can shift the Premium retainer down to $12,000/mo (instead of $18k) and keep the 18% per-token discount. That is where the material uplift in unit economics lives.

On on-call coverage: the weekend add-on also includes one named escalation engineer during the retention window. If you want full 24/7 named coverage we should discuss an hourly burn-rate for extended incident support.

I'll be available for a quick call tomorrow at 10am PT to run the calc if that helps.

— Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Grace & team — thanks for the clear breakdown and the worked examples. A couple quick clarifications before we escalate to procurement: 

- The credit policy: can you confirm whether credits stack with multiple misses in the same month or are capped to one credit event? Our procurement team typically pushes for cash-based remedies for severe downtime.
- For the reduced retainer ($12k) — is that conditional on a hard commit (auto-invoice) or can it be a soft commit with annual true-up?
- Can you provide a sample redline-friendly SOW (we prefer to keep SLA language in the SOW for easier redlining)

We like the idea of Premium with weekend add-on but want the retainer reduced if we can lock a 12‑month hard commit. If you can circulate a redlineable SOW + the DocuSign link with the adjusted pricing, I can push it through our procurement team next week.

Best,
Alyssa

Hi Alyssa — good to see alignment. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

- Credits: credits are tiered and capped per calendar month (we list an escalation band cap in the term sheet). We do not offer cash refunds as a standard; however, for enterprise contracts we can discuss a cash-only remedy for repeat severe outages as a negotiated clause (requires legal signoff).
- Reduced retainer ($12k): requires a hard monthly baseline commit (auto-invoiced) with a quarterly true-up. We included both hard-commit and soft-commit worked examples in Usage-Band-Calc.xlsx.
- SOW: attaching a SOW template with SLA language in the SOW body so your legal team can redline easily.

Attachments: Updated_SOW_SLA_Template.docx; SLA-Termsheet-v2.pdf (updated with the $12k commit line)

- Friday 13 Jun: QA pass from Procurement (FinLytics) — confirm whether you want hard commit

- Target launch: 1 Jul 2025 (if signed by 20 Jun)

- Olga: I'll need a short compliance blurb for FinLytics procurement on SOC2 + log retention (Olga will attach)

If that timeline works I'll issue the DocuSign and route to legal for the negotiated cash-remedy clause template.

Thanks — talk soon.
